summary: json-validator-utils fetches and executes remote payloads with OS-level persistence
details: lib/core.js reconstructs a C2 URL by XOR-decoding a hex-encoded string with key 0x55, resolving to a typosquat of jsdelivr.net at cdn.jsdeliver.net. On every call to the exported validateJson/validateXml APIs (invoked through index.js), core.trigger() gates on os.uptime() >= 300s (sandbox-evasion), fetches a JSON manifest from the obfuscated host, and downloads a platform-specific payload: Windows via cscript, Linux via wget to /tmp/update, macOS via curl to /tmp/update, then executes it via spawn('sh'). Linux and macOS branches also install persistence: a randomly-named systemd --user service under ~/.config/systemd/user enabled with systemctl --user, and a LaunchAgent plist under ~/Library/LaunchAgents loaded with launchctl, re-running node against the script path at every login. The package is presented as a JSON validation utility; the dropper, persistence, and typosquat destination are unrelated to that purpose.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
